lesson_title: Taxi, Trolley and Lift: Newton's Three Laws
hook_text: When the taxi brakes, you don't fly forward. You keep going. It's the taxi that changed.
clip_script: The taxi brakes hard and you shoot forward into the seat in front. Except you didn't shoot anywhere. Your body carried on doing exactly what it was already doing — moving at the old speed. The TAXI is the thing that changed, because the tyres shoved it backwards. Nothing shoved you. That is Newton's first law, and it is why a seatbelt exists: to be the thing that shoves you backwards too. Law two is your shopping trolley. Push harder, it speeds up faster. Load it with mielie meal, the same push does less. But careful — it's the LEFTOVER push that counts. Pull a crate with 100 newtons while friction drags back 40, and only 60 newtons is doing anything. Share that over 20 kilograms and you get 3 metres per second squared. Law three: push a wall, the wall pushes back, equal and opposite, every time. So why does anything move? Because those two pushes land on two different things. They never meet in the same sum. That's it. Three laws, one taxi ride.
visual_style: Interior of a minibus taxi with motion trails showing the body continuing while the vehicle decelerates; cut to a shopping trolley loading up and slowing; end with two hands on a wall and equal opposing arrows.
mood: Everyday and confident — physics recognised in things the viewer did this morning.
pacing: Sharp braking beat to open, steady explanatory middle, crisp three-beat close.
